cases.promptMarkdown:
/bg-skills:grill Plan for the order service rework. Three things are already decided:

1. Order storage moves from CRUD tables to an event-sourced log. We compared it with adding an audit table and with change data capture, and picked event sourcing because auditors must be able to replay any order's full history. Going back later would mean rebuilding every read model.
2. Orders stay in our existing Postgres cluster. It is the only database we run and nobody proposed anything else.
3. The "Export" button on the orders page gets relabelled "Download CSV".

Grill me on the rest of the plan.

The working directory is empty: no code, no `GLOSSARY.md`, no ADRs. So I can't check anything against your codebase, and I'll take your word on how the orders page works today. Here's the first round.

❓ **Q1** - **What "orders currently shown" means**: (a) only the rows on the current page; (b) every order that matches the page's current filters, search and sort, across all pages; (c) every order, ignoring filters.

➡️ (b): all orders matching the current filters and search, in the current sort order, across all pages. Staff usually filter first and then want the whole result, not just page 1.

---

❓ **Q2** - **One row per what**: (a) one CSV row per order; (b) one row per line item, with the order fields repeated on each row.

➡️ (a): one row per order. Line-item detail can be added later as a separate export if anyone asks for it.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Which columns**: (a) exactly the columns visible in the table, in the same order; (b) a fixed set of export columns, which can include fields the table doesn't show (e.g. customer email, shipping address).

➡️ (a): the export matches the table, so "what you see is what you get." That also keeps extra personal data out of files unless you choose to add it.

---

❓ **Q4** - **Who can export**: (a) anyone who can see the orders page; (b) only staff with a separate export permission.

➡️ (a): anyone who can view the orders page. They can already see the data, so a separate permission only adds admin work.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Audit trail**: should each export be logged (who, when, which filters, how many rows)? A CSV is a copy of customer data that leaves the app.

➡️ Yes: log every export with user, timestamp, filters and row count.

---

❓ **Q6** - **File format details**: UTF-8 with a BOM so Excel opens accented names correctly; comma separator; dates in ISO 8601 (`2026-11-09T14:03:00Z`); money as plain numbers plus a currency column; file named `orders-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.csv`.

➡️ Yes to all of the above.

Once I have these, the next round covers the questions that depend on Q1: size limits, and whether the download happens right away or in the background.

The *active* discipline: changing the domain model as you design, not just reading `GLOSSARY.md` for vocabulary.

## Where files live

One context: `GLOSSARY.md` at the root, ADRs in `docs/adr/`. If a root `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, it points to each context's own `GLOSSARY.md` and `docs/adr/`; system-wide ADRs stay in the root `docs/adr/`.

Create files lazily: `GLOSSARY.md` when the first term is resolved, `docs/adr/` when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

- **Challenge against the glossary.** When a term conflicts with `GLOSSARY.md`, call it out to the user at once, even when you settle it yourself: "Your glossary defines 'account' as X, but you mean Y, so I'll call Y a Z."
- **Sharpen fuzzy language.** For a vague or overloaded term, propose a precise canonical one ("Customer or User?").
- **Probe with scenarios.** Invent edge cases that force the boundaries between concepts to be exact.

## Offer ADRs sparingly

Offer an ADR only when all three hold:

1. **Hard to reverse**: changing your mind later costs something meaningful.
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will ask "why this way?"
3. **A real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives, and one was picked for specific reasons.

Missing any one, skip it. Write it using [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

# Ordering

How customers place orders and how the shop handles them until delivery.

## Language

**Order**:
A customer's request to buy one or more items, placed in a single checkout.
_Avoid_: Purchase, basket

**Line Item**:
One product and its quantity within an Order.
_Avoid_: Order line, entry

**Dispatch**:
The moment an Order leaves the warehouse.
_Avoid_: Shipping, fulfilment

**Cancellation**:
Withdrawing an entire Order before Dispatch, so nothing is sent and nothing is charged.
_Avoid_: Void, abort

**Return**:
A customer sending back one delivered Line Item after it has arrived, in exchange for a Refund of that Line Item only.
_Avoid_: Cancellation, item cancellation, cancel an item, partial cancellation

**Refund**:
Money paid back to the customer for a Returned Line Item.
_Avoid_: Reimbursement, credit

# Ordering

How customers place orders and how the shop handles them until delivery.

## Language

**Order**:
A customer's request to buy one or more items, placed in a single checkout.
_Avoid_: Purchase, basket

**Line Item**:
One product and its quantity within an Order.
_Avoid_: Order line, entry

**Dispatch**:
The moment an Order leaves the warehouse.
_Avoid_: Shipping, fulfilment

**Cancellation**:
Withdrawing an entire Order before Dispatch, so nothing is sent and nothing is charged.
Applies only to whole Orders before Dispatch; sending back a delivered Line Item is a **Return**.
_Avoid_: Void, abort

**Return**:
A customer sending back one Line Item from an Order after it has been delivered, and being refunded for that Line Item only. The rest of the Order is unaffected.
_Avoid_: Cancel an item, item cancellation, partial cancellation

How customers place orders and how the shop handles them through delivery and any Return.

## Language

**Order**:
A customer's request to buy one or more items, placed in a single checkout.

One product and its quantity within an Order.
_Avoid_: Order line, entry

_Avoid_: Cancel an item, item cancellation, partial cancellation

# Ordering

How customers place orders and how the shop handles them until delivery.

## Language

**Order**:
A customer's request to buy one or more items, placed in a single checkout.
_Avoid_: Purchase, basket

**Line Item**:
One product and its quantity within an Order.
_Avoid_: Order line, entry

**Dispatch**:
The moment an Order leaves the warehouse.
_Avoid_: Shipping, fulfilment

**Cancellation**:
Withdrawing an entire Order before Dispatch, so nothing is sent and nothing is charged.
_Avoid_: Void, abort

**Return**:
A customer sending back a single delivered Line Item and getting a refund for that Line Item only. The rest of the Order is not affected.
_Avoid_: Cancel an item, partial cancellation, item cancellation

## Relationships

- A **Cancellation** applies to a whole **Order** before **Dispatch**. A **Return** applies to one **Line Item** after it has been delivered. The two never overlap.
